title: is the unread vintage output spillover from writers whose other faces are read?

population_source.note: E472 rows are the population; this study does not re-derive the families

writer_definition: a site whose write-call evidence literals name the family token (stricter than E472's writes flag, which is any write call in a site that merely mentions the token)
method_limits: only files under results/ can be resolved; docs/ and data/ output is out of scope
a path composed at runtime from argv or a config file has no literal and is invisible
a family-token match attributes every file of that family to the writer even when several writers emit it (shared_families says so)
unread bytes are E472's family bytes divided by its vintage count, so a family whose files are uneven in size yields an average per cutoff, not a measured one
a reader that normalises the path after reading argv is counted as no consumer
